sentences.text: I'm Amelia, your host.
This podcast is for people who are learning English.
If you are an A1 level learner, don't worry.
I will speak slowly and clearly
so you can understand everything.
In today's episode, we are going to talk about Bahrain,
a small but beautiful country in the Middle East.
Part one, introduction to Bahrain.
Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf.
It is near Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Bahrain is made up of around 50 islands,
but the biggest one is called Bahrain Island.
The capital city of Bahrain is Manama.
Manama is a modern city with tall buildings, shopping malls,
and historical sites.
Many tourists visit Manama to see its markets, museums,
and the famous Bahrain World Trade Center.
Bahrain has a population of about 1.5 million people.
The official language is Arabic,
but many people also speak English,
especially in business and tourism.
Part two, geography and climate.
Bahrain is a flat country with deserts and beaches.
The country has a warm desert climate,
which means it is hot and dry for most of the year.
Summer, June, September, very hot,
with temperatures over 40 degrees with ferris.
Winter, December, February, cooler and more comfortable,
around 20 degrees, 68 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bahrain is a beautiful beach and clear blue water.
Many people go swimming and enjoy water sport.
Part three, food in Bahrain.
Bahrain has delicious food with Arabic, Persian,
and Indian influences.
Some of the most popular dishes include Moshboos,
a rice dish, and some of the most popular dishes.
Fresh with meat, spices, and vegetables.
Grilled fish, fresh fish with local spices.
Bahraini halwa, a sweet dessert made with sugar,
saffron, and nuts.
Coobs, traditional Arabic bread,
often eaten with cheese or honey.
People in Bahrain love drinking tea and coffee.
Arabic coffee, called gahwa, is served with dates
and is an important part of hospitality.
Part four, culture and traditions.
Bahrain has a rich culture and a mix
of modern and traditional life.
People enjoy music, dance, and festivals.
Traditional music.
Bahrain is famous for pearl diving songs
which were sung by fishermen in the past.
Festivals, one of the biggest celebrations
is National Day on December 16.
People celebrate with fireworks, music, and parades.
Bahrain is also known for pearl diving.
In the past, people dived into the sea to collect pearls.
And today, visitors can learn about this history.
Part five, sports, and activities.
People in Bahrain love sports.
Some of the most popular ones are, Formula One.
Bahrain has a famous Formula One race every year
at the Bahrain International Circuit.
Football, soccer, the most popular sport in the country.
Basketball, many young people enjoy playing basketball.
Basketball, water sports.
People love jet skiing, sailing, and diving.
Part six, famous places to visit.
Bahrain has many interesting places to visit.
Some of the most famous ones include,
Manama, the capital city with modern buildings
and traditional markets.
Bahrain Fort, a historical fort,
and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Manama Suke, a traditional market
with spices, jewelry, and souvenirs.
Tree of life, a 400 year old tree
that grows in the middle of the desert.
Al-Arene Wildlife Park,
a park where you can see camels, deer, and flamingos.
Closing, that's all for today's episode.
I hope you learned something new about Bahrain.
It is a small but amazing country
with rich history, beautiful beaches, and delicious food.
If you ever have the chance to visit, make sure to.
Try Moshboos and Bahraini Halwa.
Watch a Formula One race.
Visit the Tree of Life.
